Thanks for the quick turnaround. The proposal looks good overall but two items are blockers for our CFO / procurement:

2) The VPC add-on cost is higher than expected; can you provide a one-time deployment credit or reduce the add-on rate for the pilot?

Subject: Fwd: Crestline ask — two-month credit + VPC concession (need VP/CFO signoff)

Marissa / Rishi —

Looping you in. Crestline is asking for:
- Extend onboarding credit to cover month 1 and month 2 (effectively doubling the credit).
- A one-time concession to offset the private VPC deployment fee for the pilot (they requested reduction of the add-on).

Deal context: Strategic health system, likely to convert to a Dedicated deployment after pilot; expected ARR if closed post-pilot ~ $420k ARR. Procurement is ready to sign if we can confirm economics this week.

I ran a quick margin calc: incremental cost of temporary VPC staging is modest for the pilot (small infra uplift). Primary impact is precedent for future VPC concessions in mid-market health customers.

Can you advise next steps? I can draft a concise exception memo for Markus (CFO) if you want a formal ask.

Laura
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Crestline ask — two-month credit + VPC concession (need VP/CFO signoff)

Laura —

Thanks for the context. I agree this is strategically important. Two quick notes:
- Two-month onboarding credit is reasonable if we tie it to measurable KPIs (deploy + model quality gates). Add a line in the SOW for acceptance criteria.
- One-time VPC deployment concession: I can approve up to a 60% deployment credit for pilot (one-time) but we need executive signoff for anything beyond that. Rishi, can you prepare an exception memo that quantifies net NPV impact and sets guardrails (e.g., no blanket VPC discounts moving forward; this is pilot-only, non-transferable)?

Markus — please confirm if CFO signature is required for the 60% concession or if this can be handled at VP level (Marissa) given the strategic upside.

— Marissa
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: MarkUs Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exception memo: Crestline Health pilot VPC concession & extended onboarding credit

Markus —

Attached is a short exception memo (exception-memo-crst-9-16.pdf) requesting CFO signoff for the proposed concessions to Crestline Health. Summary: 
- Request: 60% one-time credit on VPC pilot deployment fee (estimated list: $18,000; discounted pilot charge: $7,200).
- Request: Extend onboarding credit to cover month 1 + month 2 (existing proposal: 25% credit month 1. Proposed: 25% month 1 + 25% month 2).
- Commercial rationale: Crestline is a top-4 regional health system; pilot likely to convert to Dedicated in H1 2027 with projected ARR ~$420k. The probability-weighted value (at 55% conversion pro forma) yields expected NPV materially positive vs. pilot concession.
- Guardrails: Concessions apply only to this pilot, non-precedential, require SOW language with acceptance criteria and no transfer to other business units. Any future VPC concessions must go through Commercial Strategy + Finance review.

Net financial impact: one-time revenue concession ~ $10,800; expected lifetime value retained > $230k (conservative).

Please reply with signoff or suggested changes. If approved, we will: 1) update the proposal PDF, 2) send DocuSign to Crestline, 3) treasury will mark the deal for discounted pilot billing.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Exception memo: Crestline Health pilot VPC concession & extended onboarding credit

Rishi / Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for the memo and clear guardrails. I reviewed the numbers and the strategic rationale. I approve the exceptions as requested with the following conditions:
1) Add explicit acceptance criteria to SOW (three production prompts, latency targets, and quality thresholds).
2) Set the pilot term to 6 weeks and cap total discounted pilot spend at $12k (inclusive of credits).
3) Legal should add an explicit non-precedent clause to the SOW and Procurement playbook should be notified.

Rishi — please publish the final version of the exception memo with these conditions and loop Legal for the SOW language. Laura — you can communicate approval to Crestline and send the updated proposal + DocuSign.

Markus Klein
VP Finance (Interim CFO) | Redwood Inference
